transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:30 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Kim (CISO, Lumen), Rajesh Nair (Head of Infra), Emily Stone (Cloud Security Engineer)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya at Redwood, AE on this account, and I've got Ethan from our security/infra team. We're hoping to understand Lumen's security posture and any must-haves for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:12] Sarah: Hi, thanks Maya. Quick intro — I'm Sarah, CISO. Rajesh is our infra lead, Emily's on cloud security. We're exploring LLM infra for R&D workflows but security is the gating factor.
[00:24] Ethan: Great, can you run through your top concerns so we can be specific?
[00:30] Rajesh: Sure. High level: auditability and retention of logs, KMS/HSM integration for customer keys, SSO and SCIM for onboarding, RBAC granularity, and compliance artifacts — SOC 2, ISO 27001 scope. Also data residency, we have EU and US datasets.
[00:45] Maya: Perfect. We'll cover each. Quick note — I'll drop links to our SOC 2 and ISO summaries after the call, and Ethan will talk to integration details.

--- Topics: SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS/HSM, data retention / residency ---

[01:10] Ethan: On SOC 2, Redwood has a Type II. We can provide the summary report and a redacted copy on an NDA. For ISO, we maintain ISO 27001 controls for our private deployments — scope is mainly control plane and customer-managed data plane for private.
[01:28] Sarah: When you say "private deployments" is that the VPC/on-prem package? Who holds the keys there?
[01:36] Ethan: For Private (VPC/on-prem), customers can bring-your-own-KMS or integrate with their HSM. Key ownership and KMS are customer-managed; for Hosted we use envelope encryption — customer keys via KMS integrations are possible on Dedicated and Private tiers. There was a small hiccup in one earlier transcript where we said "KV cash" — that's KV cache, sorry, transcription thing.
[01:54] Emily: So for Hosted, do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) or just Redwood keys?
[02:00] Ethan: Hosted generally uses our managed KMS but we offer a BYOK path for enterprise customers on Dedicated and Private. For strict compliance, private with BYOK+HSM is the pattern we recommend.

[02:18] Rajesh: What's the model for SAML/SSO and SCIM? We need group sync and role mappings into RBAC.
[02:25] Maya: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC and SCIM provisioning for user sync. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles — and roles are pretty granular (admin, dev, ops, read-only, etc.).
[02:40] Emily: Is RBAC enforced at the token/request level? We need least privilege so ops scripts can't call model-management APIs.
[02:48] Ethan: Yes, RBAC is enforced at the API layer. Tokens are scoped — we issue tokens tied to routes and models. You can also configure per-model and per-route ACLs. We surfaced that in the console and via IAM APIs.

[03:05] Sarah: Audit logs — we need immutable logs exportable to our SIEM with retention options up to 7 years. Can Redwood stream audit logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
[03:17] Ethan: We support log streaming to customer endpoints (S3, syslog, Kinesis) and direct connectors to common SIEMs. Audit logs include admin actions, model deployments, API calls, and token-level metadata. Retention varies by plan; for enterprise dedicated/private we can configure long-term retention and export policies.
[03:36] Maya: I'll attach an example log export schema and sample event later — the team asked to see field names.

[03:45] Rajesh: Encryption in transit and at rest? Also hardware security modules?
[03:50] Ethan: TLS 1.2+ for transit. At rest we use AES-256. For key management, Dedicated and Private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We also support HSM-backed signing for critical ops. If you need FIPS/HSM attestation, we can discuss Private on-prem.

[04:10] Emily: Can we rotate keys without downtime?
[04:13] Ethan: Yes, key rotation is supported. With BYOK, rotation happens via the KMS with zero-downtime model; we maintain layered envelope encryption to avoid re-encrypting huge datasets.

[04:25] Sarah: Data residency — we have EU-only projects. If we go hosted, can you guarantee EU data stays in EU?
[04:33] Maya: Hosted customers can pick region; we have EU regions and we can scope datasets to region. For strict residency guarantees and air-gapped requirements we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem).

[04:45] Rajesh: Any SOC 2 carve-outs or open items we should be aware of?
[04:50] Ethan: No major carve-outs. The usual is that for Private deployments some controls shift to the customer — like physical security on on-prem hardware. We'll highlight shared responsibility in the doc.

[05:02] Emily: What's your incident response and breach notification SLA?
[05:06] Maya: We have a Standard incident response playbook and we notify customers per contract SLAs — typically 72 hours for confirmed breaches, with escalations for critical incidents. For Dedicated/Private we can negotiate tighter SLAs in the contract.

[05:22] Rajesh: Perf/security tradeoffs — we'd like to do a dedicated pilot to validate both latency and that audit logs capture the request/response without PII leaking.
[05:33] Ethan: That's reasonable. The pilot would run on a dedicated pool; we can enable full request/response auditing (with PII redaction rules) and feed logs to your SIEM. We'll provide a runbook.

[05:46] Sarah: Are prompts and model requests stored? Retention defaults and deletion?
[05:51] Ethan: By default hosted stores request logs short-term for observability; you can opt into longer retention or disable storage. On Dedicated/Private you can configure storage policies; Private with customer-managed storage means you control deletion. We'll provide the retention policy matrix.

[06:10] Emily: For regulatory audits, can you produce exports of requests tied to an account for a given date range?
[06:16] Ethan: Yes, audit exports by tenant/account/time range are supported — export to S3. For PII-sensitive requests we recommend enabling redaction and also routing logs directly to your storage so Redwood doesn't retain copies.

[06:30] Maya: Quick check — are there any blockers we haven't touched?
[06:34] Sarah: Mainly proof: SOC2 artifacts, sample audit log with schema, proof of BYOK/HSM integration, and geography guarantees. Also pricing for the Dedicated pilot.
[06:45] Maya: Great — we'll send the SOC2 summary, sample log schema, and a pilot pricing estimate. Ethan will own the pilot runbook.

[06:54] Rajesh: A couple more technicals — network egress controls, private endpoints for APIs, and our compliance team will want SAML sign-on enforceable with MFA.
[07:03] Ethan: We support private endpoints (VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents), and you can enforce MFA at IdP level. Network egress rules can be locked down; we'll provide a whitelist approach and egress flows for model artifacts.

[07:20] Emily: Any limitations on model artifacts storage, like KV cache or keys persisted? We want to ensure caches aren't persisted to shared storage.
[07:29] Ethan: KV cache is memory-first and by default ephemeral; for persistent cache in Dedicated you'll get isolated storage. We can document how caches are isolated per tenant.

[07:40] Maya: I'll also include our security whitepaper and a link to the private deployment datasheet: https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper (note: link shared).

[07:50] Sarah: Good. For the pilot scope: 1) Dedicated pool in us-east or eu-west, 2) BYOK/KMS test, 3) audit log streaming to our S3, 4) token-scoped RBAC test cases.
[08:04] Ethan: We'll map test cases to runbook steps and provide the benchmark sheet (latency p50/p95, cost estimates).

[08:12] Maya: Anything else?
[08:15] Rajesh: Contract questions — what T&Cs for data processing and DPA?
[08:19] Maya: We have a standard DPA and data processing addendum. For enterprise deals we can negotiate additional terms. I'll have legal send a copy.

[08:28] Sarah: Okay that's it from us. Appreciate the details.
[08:32] Maya: Thanks everyone. Recap: we'll send SOC2, ISO summary, sample logs, pilot runbook & pricing. We'll aim to get artifacts over by Friday.
[08:42] Ethan: I'll set up a follow-up to kick off the pilot and share the benchmark workbook.
[08:48] Sarah: Sounds good. We'll review and circle back with stakeholders.

--- End transcript ---

Notes: Transcript has occasional transcription errors (proper nouns, acronyms). Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper, (SOC2 summary link to be emailed), pilot-runbook (internal doc link to be shared).
